LESSON: ELECTRICAL ENERGY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 4.1: Electrical Energy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Electrical Energy, part of Force and Energy in Grade 7 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: What are the sources of electricity in the environment? 2. How is electricity used in day-to- day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the sources of electricity in the environment,

2. use print or digital media to search for more information on sources of electricity in nature (hydro-electric power, geothermal, solar, wind power, nuclear, tidal-wave, fossil fuels, biomass, natural gas, electrical cells),

3. collaboratively set up simple electrical circuits in series and in parallel (using electrical cells, connecting wires, switch, bulb, bulb holder) to demonstrate the flow of electric current,

4. discuss common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life (pressure cooker, electric cooker, electric blender, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the sources of electricity in the environment,
2. use print or digital media to search for more information on sources of electricity in nature (hydro-electric power, geothermal, solar, wind power, nuclear, tidal-wave, fossil fuels, biomass, natural gas, electrical cells),
3. collaboratively set up simple electrical circuits in series and in parallel (using electrical cells, connecting wires, switch, bulb, bulb holder) to demonstrate the flow of electric current,
4. discuss common electrical appliances used in day-to-day life (pressure cooker, electric cooker, electric blender, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Electrical Energy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: the learner learns how to set up a simple electric circuit as they carry out activities of series

and parallel circuits.

● Communication and Collaboration: the learner collaboratively works with peers to set up simple electrical

circuits in series and parallel.

Values:
• Unity: the learner with peers harmoniously set up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel.

• Responsibility: the learner practises carefully handles various apparatus as they set up simple electrical circuits in series and

parallel while working.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate concepts in electrical circuits to electrical energy in Pre-Technical Studies
